page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is an ARM64-based server instance belonging to the Dpldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor, with one thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 2835 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled, though it lacks AVX, AMX, and hyper-threading capabilities.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in large-block uncached memory bandwidth read operations at 464.03 GB/sec and write operations at 200.4 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score and database operations score. Multi-core processing is highly competitive, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching the top-tier category and stress-ng multi-core performance in the strong category. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and PassMark CPU scores falling within the average category.

The instance exhibits a low memory-to-core ratio, which represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications but enhances cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. In LLM inference, performance varies; text generation with a medium 7B model is strong, whereas text generation with a small 135M model and prompt processing for a large 70B model fall into the weak category. Given its high-speed local NVMe storage, strong database operations, and high static web serving throughput, the server is suited for multi-threaded application hosting, database operations, software compilation, and web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is an ARM64-based virtual machine from the Dpldsv6 family, featuring 48 dedicated physical cores on a 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. Equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM and a 2835 GB local NVMe SSD, this instance is optimized for compute-heavy workloads. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in large-block memory bandwidth and database operations, alongside strong multi-core execution in Geekbench and stress-ng. However, single-core metrics and certain LLM inference tasks remain in the average to weak categories. The lack of hyper-threading and AVX support represents a clear architectural tradeoff. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving where local storage and high memory bandwidth are critical.
